prTitle: fix(checks): recognize covered cancelled duplicate runs
prBody:
Duplicate pull-request workflow runs can receive IDs in a different order from when their checks execute. A higher-ID cancelled duplicate previously kept Shepherd failing even after the matching lower-ID check started later and succeeded.

Recognize that cancellation as superseded when a completed successful check from a distinct lower-ID run has the same workflow ID, event, check name, and commit scope, with strictly later valid start and completion timestamps. Compact polling now requests and maps those timestamps. Event and commit boundaries also constrain the existing higher-ID supersession rule, and PR-head and merge-queue rollups are classified separately.

Timing establishes observed check coverage rather than proof that both triggers tested an identical PR base. Uncertain metadata, unmatched cancellations, pending checks, and genuine failures retain their blocking behavior.

Validation: 3,520 tests passed across 501 files with 100% line coverage; lint, typecheck, format check, and build passed. Includes four CLI scenarios with reviewed JSON/Markdown snapshots: covered cancellation, pending work, genuine failure, and unmatched cancellation.

Refs https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/issues/1991

<details>
<summary>Shepherd Journal</summary>

- minimized 1 comment as @jonathanong (rule: coderabbit review-in-progress notice): https://github.com/jonathanong/pr-shepherd/pull/505#issuecomment-5983804583
- Reviewed [Sourcery guide](https://github.com/jonathanong/pr-shepherd/pull/505#issuecomment-5983804537) and review PRR_kwDOSGizTs8AAAABQlX7yA: guide informational; review budget exhausted, no findings supplied. Local independent review and 3,519 tests completed. Timestamp ordering is evidence of later check execution, not proof of identical tested base revisions.
- Fixed [CodeRabbit queue-event finding](https://github.com/jonathanong/pr-shepherd/pull/505#discussion_r4179103052) in ab245ec: compact polling accepts merge_group only for queue rollups, with a head-versus-queue regression test. Full validation: 3,520 tests, 100% line coverage, lint, typecheck, format, and build passed.
</details>

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Surface timestamp evidence instead of classifying it**

When a lower-ID success has later timestamps, this predicate silently changes the cancellation to `superseded`; `getCiVerdict` then excludes it from failures and may report `allPassed`, while the agent output exposes only the check name in `supersededNames`, not the timestamps, workflow/event, or candidate run that justified suppression. This makes the CLI interpret hidden raw GitHub data—and potentially advance the PR—rather than letting the agent evaluate the evidence, so surface that context instead of deriving this category.

## Reviewer's Guide The PR fixes false blocking from cancelled duplicate workflow runs by combining same-context higher-run-ID detection with strict timestamp-based evidence that a lower-ID run actually executed later, propagating chronology through compact polling while preserving failures, uncertainty, pending work, and cross-context boundaries. #### Sequence diagram for timestamp-based cancelled run coverage ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Poll as Compact polling participant Classifier as Check classifier participant Cancelled as Higher-ID cancelled run participant Success as Lower-ID successful run participant Verdict as Shepherd verdict Poll->>Poll: parseCreatedAt(startedAt, completedAt) Poll->>Classifier: classifyChecks(checks) Classifier->>Cancelled: validate numeric runId and timestamps Classifier->>Success: compare workflowId, event, scope, commitOid, name Success-->>Classifier: SUCCESS with later startedAtUnix and completedAtUnix Classifier->>Verdict: classify cancelled check as superseded Verdict-->>Poll: non-blocking superseded result ``` #### Flow diagram for cancelled check supersession classification ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Cancelled check] --> B{Same workflow event scope commit?} B -->|yes| C{Higher numeric run ID exists?} C -->|yes| S[Superseded] C -->|no| D{Matching lower-ID success exists?} B -->|no| D D -->|yes| E[Same workflow ID and exact check name] E -->|yes| F[Later valid start and completion timestamps] F -->|yes| S D -->|no| X[Failing] E -->|no| X F -->|no| X ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Expand cancelled-check supersession to account for observed execution order, while tightening identity and context boundaries. |
